content:
Unit 3 - Evidence-Based Questions — Title & Goal
Learn to master unit 3 - evidence-based questions questions for the Digital SAT through a short concept, a modeled item, and targeted practice.

Key skill

Read the note and focus on what the question is really asking inside the passage.

  • Locate explicit claims and implicit ideas.
  • Ask: What is the passage mainly doing?
  • Match answers to the most general accurate statement.

Model item

Study how the evidence in the passage supports the correct answer.

Passage — The article states that park attendance rose after new lighting was installed, and later notes that evening events drew families who previously avoided the park.

Question 1. Which choice best supports the claim that lighting improvements increased community use?

  • ‘attendance rose after new lighting was installed’
  • ‘the park opened at sunrise’
  • ‘some residents prefer morning walks’
  • ‘the city considered building a new park’
A directly ties the improvement to increased attendance.

Quick practice

Try these quickly. Eliminate two choices before choosing your answer.

Passage — The report argues that replacing older boilers cut fuel costs ‘by nearly a third.’

Question 2. Which quotation best supports the claim that the replacements saved money?

  • ‘replacing older boilers’
  • ‘cut fuel costs by nearly a third’
  • ‘during the winter months’
  • ‘maintenance was scheduled’
B directly states the savings.

Passage — The biologist concludes that the species returned to the region after wetlands were restored.

Question 3. Which line best supports the conclusion?

  • ‘wetlands were restored’
  • ‘the species returned to the region’
  • ‘sightings increased following restoration’
  • ‘the region receives heavy rainfall’
C links return to timing after restoration → causal support.

Next skill

Build on the previous skill. Compare how this question type reads the passage differently.

Note: Locate the exact phrase or sentence that proves your choice.

Another model item

Notice how small wording differences change the best answer.

Passage — A newsletter claims that adding bike lanes reduced downtown traffic congestion during peak hours.

Question 4. Which statement best supports the claim?

  • ‘peak-hour speeds increased by 12%’
  • ‘weekend markets are popular’
  • ‘some drivers prefer side streets’
  • ‘rainy days reduce biking’
A is direct, quantifiable evidence consistent with reduced congestion.

More practice

Aim for accuracy first, then speed. Re-check the evidence that rules out each wrong choice.

Passage — The principal argues that tutoring expanded access for students who could not stay after school.

Question 5. Which line best supports the principal’s claim?

  • ‘sessions began before first period’
  • ‘tutoring rooms were painted’
  • ‘attendance rules were updated’
  • ‘students ate breakfast in the cafeteria’

Mixed practice set

These mix multiple skills. Mark the question type before you start, then solve.

Passage — The memo argues for investing in energy-efficient windows to reduce heating costs.

Question 6. Which sentence best supports the memo’s proposal?

  • ‘winter temperatures vary by region’
  • ‘the new windows reduced heat loss by 28% in a pilot wing’
  • ‘construction took two weeks’
  • ‘staff moved to temporary offices’
